title: Flight surgeon gum exam, burns and skin samples while OSI watched
place_text: Flight surgeon's office, Ellsworth AFB, South Dakota

He went up here and he just clipped a piece of skin off there and he took the whole tool and he stuck it right down in there and put a cork on it, laid it on that tray.
tellings.difference: Describes the skin being clipped and corked in a tube on the tray.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the flight surgeon taking skin samples from Mario at Ellsworth in 1977 while OSI watched.

as_told.title: Flight surgeon takes a skin tissue sample from Mario

plain: A former Air Force nuclear weapons guard named Mario Woods says that in 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a flight surgeon (a military doctor) examined him while agents of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the service's own investigators, looked on. Woods says the doctor checked his gums, pointed out burns above his right eye and on the back of his right hand, and clipped off a piece of skin, which he sealed in a corked tube and set on a tray. Woods tells this himself, in two separate conversations with Michels, as part of what he describes as an abduction, and if true it would mean the military took a close interest in what happened to him.
